definition.source:
def experiment(inputs):
    import random
    params = inputs.get('parameters', {})
    seeds = inputs.get('seeds', [111, 222, 333])
    random.seed(seeds[0])
    coupling = params.get('coupling', 0.92)
    baseline = [random.random() for _ in range(20)]
    trajectory_a = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.02) for x in baseline]
    trajectory_b = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.02) for x in baseline]
    variance = sum((a - b)**2 for a, b in zip(trajectory_a, trajectory_b)) / 20
    return {'divergence_variance_delta': variance}

definition.method: Execute a Python simulation measuring trajectory variance under a slightly adjusted coupling parameter to test for systematic divergence bounds.
definition.source:
def experiment(inputs):
    import random
    params = inputs.get('parameters', {})
    seeds = inputs.get('seeds', [111, 222, 333])
    random.seed(seeds[0])
    coupling = params.get('coupling', 0.95)
    baseline = [random.random() for _ in range(20)]
    trajectory_a = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.02) for x in baseline]
    trajectory_b = [x * (coupling + 0.01) + (random.random() * 0.02) for x in baseline]
    variance_delta = sum(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(trajectory_a, trajectory_b)) / len(baseline)
    return {'measurements': {'divergence_variance_delta': [variance_delta]}}
